title: Remove all whitespace from a string using `chars().filter(c -> !Character.isWhitespace(c))` and `Collectors.joining()`.
shortTitle: Remove all whitespace from a string using chars().filter and Collectors.joining()

s1_definition.profdef: You stream the characters, filter out whitespace with `!Character.isWhitespace(c)`, map each surviving code point to a single-character string, and collect with `Collectors.joining()` to rebuild a whitespace-free string.
s1_definition.analogy: Priya takes a messy code with spaces and tabs and squeezes out every blank, leaving only the real characters packed together.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** You stream the characters, filter out whitespace with `!Character.isWhitespace(c)`, map each surviving code point to a single-character string, and collect with `Collectors.joining()` to rebuild a whitespace-free string.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** Priya takes a messy code with spaces and tabs and squeezes out every blank, leaving only the real characters packed together.

**One line to remember:** `chars().filter(c -> !isWhitespace(c)).mapToObj(c->String.valueOf((char)c)).collect(joining())` strips whitespace.

sections.s2_technical:
`s.chars()` gives an IntStream of code points. `filter(c -> !Character.isWhitespace(c))` keeps only non-whitespace characters, where `isWhitespace` covers spaces, tabs, newlines, and other Unicode whitespace. You then `mapToObj(c -> String.valueOf((char) c))` to turn each code into a one-character string and `collect(Collectors.joining())` to concatenate them with no separator.

The result is the original string with all whitespace removed. An alternative is simply `s.replaceAll("\\s+", "")`, which is shorter, but the stream approach is instructive and lets you plug in any character predicate, not just whitespace. joining with no argument concatenates with nothing between, which is exactly what rebuilding a string needs.

The senior nuance is that `Character.isWhitespace` is Unicode-aware and broader than just the space character, which matters for real input with tabs or non-breaking contexts. For production I often prefer the regex `replaceAll` for brevity, but the stream version shines when the filtering rule is more complex than whitespace. I also note that mapping each char to a String then joining is the standard way to convert an IntStream of characters back into a String.
sections.s3_banking:
Problem 1 — Account reference codes arrive at the National Bank of India with accidental spaces and tabs, which must be stripped before validation and storage.

This is exactly what filter-whitespace plus joining does — it removes every whitespace character and rebuilds a clean code.

The code defines a `SanitizeService.stripWhitespace` method and a demo.
sections.s5_journey:
Input: the messy code "SAV 2001\t " with a space, a tab, and a trailing space.

Step 1: chars streams every character including the space, digits, the tab, and the trailing space.

Step 2: filter drops the space, the tab, and the trailing space because isWhitespace is true for them.

Step 3: mapToObj turns each surviving character into a one-character string.

Step 4: joining concatenates them with nothing between, giving "SAV2001".

```
INFO: stream : 'SAV2001'
INFO: regex  : 'SAV2001'
```
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  "SAV 2001\t "
    │ chars()
    │ filter(!isWhitespace)   ← drops ' ', '\t', trailing ' '
    │ mapToObj(String.valueOf((char)))
    │ joining()
    ▼
  "SAV2001"
```

sections.s6_takeaway:
To strip all whitespace with streams I take the characters with chars, filter out whitespace using the negation of Character is whitespace, map each surviving code point to a one-character string, and collect with the no-argument joining, which concatenates them with nothing between and rebuilds a clean string. For a code like SAV space 2001 tab, this drops the space and the tab and the trailing space to give SAV2001.

I rely on Character is whitespace because it is Unicode-aware and catches far more than the plain space character — tabs, newlines, and other whitespace forms — which matters for real input at the National Bank of India where account codes arrive with accidental spacing before validation and storage. Mapping each char to a String and then joining is the standard idiom for turning an IntStream of characters back into a String.

The senior point I add is that for the specific case of whitespace I often reach for the concise regex replaceAll of backslash s plus with an empty string, which is shorter and perfectly clear. The stream version earns its keep when the filtering rule is more complex than whitespace — say, keeping only digits and letters — because then I just swap the predicate, and the same filter-map-join shape rebuilds the sanitised string.
